decisions.reason: The old biconditional admits a record taking 1 J in and sending 1 J out although thermal transfer occurs. The repaired Definition supplies nonnegative cumulative incoming/outgoing thermal energies on each process interval, defines Q as their terminal difference, and requires both histories to vanish for adiabaticity. This repairs the false class identification while retaining the core-only first-law scope.

reviews.reason: Reviewed the typed tuple, endpoint maps, core mass/energy restrictions and actual suppliers. Each supplied heat history is finite, nonnegative, starts at zero and has nonnegative increments. Its prescribed interpretation counts all incoming or outgoing outer-boundary thermal transfer before cancellation. Requiring both histories to vanish excludes sequential and simultaneous cancelling thermal exchanges; Q=0 remains a necessary consequence. Configuration regularity, work signs, transfer-map domain and statistical-preparation qualifications are preserved. This is the author review of the repair, not independent acceptance.
